The owner should check each claim against what the app actually does.
Colour names are not checked against the stylesheet here.

terms.meaning: The first page a visitor sees when they arrive at the site.
A named AI analyst with its own style and tool.
A named colour value, such as a variable in the stylesheet, that the page uses by name.

sections.name: SportKey, PersonaKey
sections.title: Allowed sport and analyst names
sections.what: Lists the five sports and the five analyst names allowed in this copy.
sections.why: Stops a typo in the copy from reaching the page as an unknown name.
sections.watch_out: These names must match the analyst card files and the sport list elsewhere, or they will drift apart.

sections.name: ROSTER_COPY
sections.title: Analyst descriptions
sections.what: Gives each of the five analysts a short motto and a one-line description of their signature tool.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives each analyst a short public identity on the landing page.
sections.watch_out: The tool names should match the signature tool on each analyst card.

sections.name: LIVE_NOW
sections.title: Features that ship today
sections.what: Three cards for features described as live: private groups, how calls are graded, and cricket scores. Each has a title, a text, a link and a button label.
sections.why: Lists only what works, so visitors are not promised unfinished features.
sections.watch_out: The cricket card says scores are delayed, so this wording must change if the source changes.

sections.name: IN_DEVELOPMENT
sections.title: Features still being built
sections.what: Three cards for features not yet ready: the Decision Lab, The Desk and the alter ego feature.
sections.why: Shows plans without implying that they work.
sections.watch_out: Moving one of these to the live list needs the feature to really work, since the copy alone proves nothing.

sections.name: PRINCIPLES
sections.title: Product promises shown to visitors
sections.what: Four principles: every number links to its source, calls are graded on the decision not the luck, no money changes hands, and data states are always labelled honestly. Each has a colour name.
sections.why: Sets public promises the team has to keep.
sections.watch_out: The colour names must exist in the stylesheet, or the colours will not show.

summary: The fixed wording for the landing page: analyst descriptions, what is live, what is in development, and the product promises.
purpose: It keeps the public copy in one file, and it separates shipped features from planned ones.
why: Keeps the page honest about what works, and lets wording change without touching page layout.
how: It defines the allowed sport and analyst names, gives each analyst a short motto and tool description, then lists the live features, the features in development, and the four principles with their colour names.
inputs: Not applicable: the file holds fixed text.
outputs: Text and lists that the landing page displays.
risks: Any claim written here becomes a public promise. A feature moved to the live list before it works would mislead visitors.
debug: If the page shows the wrong wording, check this file first. If a colour does not appear, check that the colour name exists in the stylesheet.
